inventory.value: Translate gastrointestinal function, access, formula composition, medication handling, and monitoring into a safe enteral nutrition plan.

inventory.value: Determine when enteral nutrition is appropriate and when feeding should be delayed or withheld.
inventory.support: Book inadequate intake/usable GI tract; dated2016 B1/B5/C1/C3 and safe2017Q1.1/Q4.1; indication competency, no numeric timing rule.

inventory.value: Select an access site and administration method that match duration, gastric function, aspiration risk, and patient goals.
inventory.support: Book NG/PEG/PEJ destination/duration; safe2017Q4.1/Q6.7 and2016B4a/b,D4a/b; individualized access/schedule competency.

inventory.value: Compare formula composition and calculate delivery, free water, and supplemental flush requirements.
inventory.support: Book labeled EN composition and volume/rate arithmetic; safe2017Q2.4/Q5.1/Q5.2/Q7.2; calculated water and total fluid competency.

inventory.value: Administer medications through enteral access without compromising the drug, formula, or tube.
inventory.support: Book solid/liquid compatibility, altered exposure and blockage; safe2017Q8.1/Q8.2; safe-administration competency, not guarantee of absence of harm.

inventory.value: Recognize signs that warrant assessment for intolerance, refeeding risk, aspiration, contamination, or mechanical complications.
inventory.support: Safe2017Q6.9/Q11.1,2016D1/D2/D4/D6 and2020adultTable6; assessment competency, no automatic symptom attribution.

inventory.value: The Enteral Decision
inventory.support: Editorial heading matched to reviewed lesson topics.

inventory.value: Use the gastrointestinal tract when it can safely receive and absorb nutrients, but separate a functioning gut from a patient who is not yet adequately resuscitated.
inventory.support: Book GI use plus2016B5 full resuscitation/stability scope; safe2017Q4.1 access suitability.

inventory.value: Indications and goals
inventory.support: Book oral inadequacy plus safe2017Q1.1/Table1 assessment and2016B1.

inventory.value: Hemodynamic stability
inventory.support: 2016B5 recommendation and whole rationale; stability/resuscitation before start or restart.

inventory.value: Contraindications
inventory.support: 2016B5 suspected ischemia/instability and safe2017Q4.1; complete intestinal obstruction distinguished from selected gastric-outlet bypass.

inventory.value: Early critical care feeding
inventory.support: 2016B1/C1/C3 with low-risk exception and monitored advancement, not universal full-rate feeding.

inventory.value: Before writing a feeding order, state why oral intake is inadequate, whether the gut is usable, whether perfusion is adequate, and what clinical outcome the therapy should support.
inventory.support: Safe2017Q1.1 and2016B1/B5/C1/C3: assess oral intake, usable gut, perfusion and goals before order.

inventory.value: A functional, safe gut supports enteral nutrition; compare routes within the applicable clinical setting.
inventory.support: Book gut use qualified by2022ASPEN Q3 clinical population/first-week route comparison.

inventory.value: Nutrition risk and expected inadequacy guide initiation.
inventory.support: 2016B1/C1/C3 and safe2017Q1.1 nutrition risk and expected inadequate intake.

inventory.value: Withhold feeding for suspected bowel ischemia, complete intestinal obstruction, or hemodynamic instability; reassess before initiation or resumption.
inventory.support: 2016B5 hold until resuscitated/stable and on possible gut ischemia; safe2017Q4.1 contraindications. Reassessment does not itself authorize unsafe resumption.

inventory.value: Early feeding is a monitored strategy, not an automatic full-rate order.
inventory.support: 2016B1/C1/C3 and2020adultTable6 refeeding/tolerance constraints; no numeric advancement adopted.

inventory.value: Access and Route Selection
inventory.support: Editorial heading matched to reviewed lesson topics.

inventory.value: Access is chosen by expected duration, anatomy, gastric emptying, aspiration risk, procedural burden, and the therapies that must pass through the tube.
inventory.support: Book short versus longer access/destinations; safe2017Q4.1/Q8.1 and2016B4a/b,D4a/b: anatomy/function, tolerance, aspiration and medication requirements.

inventory.value: Gastric versus postpyloric
inventory.support: Book destination diagram; safe2017Q4.1 and2016B4a/b.

inventory.value: Nasal versus percutaneous
inventory.support: Book NG/PEG/PEJ diagram and expected duration; safe2017Q4.1.

inventory.value: Placement confirmation
inventory.support: Safe2017Q4.4/Q4.5 age-specific confirmation and reassessment.

inventory.value: ENFit safety
inventory.support: Safe2017Q9.3/Figure11 and FDA2015I/II/III/V.A/V.D-F; engineering prevention, no mandate or measured reduction claim.

inventory.value: Choose the least invasive route that can reliably deliver the prescribed therapy, then build a placement, securement, skin care, and reassessment plan around it.
inventory.support: Safe2017Q4.1 appropriately selected feasible access, Q4.4/Q4.5 confirmation, Q4.6 securement and Section10/Q11.1 care/reassessment; least-invasive choice still must reliably deliver therapy.

inventory.value: Gastric access permits bolus, intermittent, or continuous feeding when function, tolerance, and aspiration risk allow.
inventory.support: Safe2017 completeQ6.7 schedule rationale and2016B4a/b,D4a/b patient/tolerance/aspiration qualifications.

inventory.value: Postpyloric access is selected for a clinical reason, not by habit.
inventory.support: Safe2017Q4.1 and2016B4a/b clinical selection for gastroparesis/intolerance or aspiration risk.

inventory.value: Confirm initial placement before use and reassess possible migration.
inventory.support: Safe2017Q4.4/Q4.5/Q6.2 confirmation and possible migration assessment.

inventory.value: Use enteral-specific connectors to reduce the risk of wrong-route connections.
inventory.support: FDA2015I/II and safe2017Q9.3 design to prevent enteral-to-nonenteral connection; intent rather than unmeasured event reduction.

inventory.value: Delivery and the Feeding Prescription
inventory.support: Editorial heading matched to reviewed lesson topics.

inventory.value: The prescription links a daily nutrient and fluid target to a formula, route, rate, schedule, flush plan, and advancement strategy.
inventory.support: Safe2017Q2.4 prescription components, Q6.7 schedules and2020adultTable6 advancement; book rate/volume accounting.

inventory.value: Bolus, intermittent, and continuous delivery
inventory.support: Safe2017Q6.7 individual schedules and2016D4b aspiration/bolus tolerance.

inventory.value: Daily volume targets
inventory.support: Book delivered/labeled amount plus safe2017Q2.4/Q6.7 prescribed-volume goals.

inventory.value: Rate calculations
inventory.support: Book volume divided by actual running hours; previously independently calculated examples retained.

inventory.value: Advancement and interruptions
inventory.support: Safe2017Q6.7 interruptions and2020adultTable6 refeeding advancement constraints.

inventory.value: Every order should make the intended daily volume visible. Calculate what will actually be delivered after holds, procedures, medication windows, and pump downtime.
inventory.support: Safe2017Q6.7/Q6.11 scheduling and measurement; book actual volume accounting. No automatic catch-up above prescribed limits.

inventory.value: Bolus feeding is generally a gastric strategy.
inventory.support: Safe2017Q6.7 gastric meal-like bolus options and2016D4b high-risk controlled continuous option; generally qualification retained.

inventory.value: Rate multiplied by hours equals delivered volume.
inventory.support: Book dimensional arithmetic: mL/h times h gives mL; verified examples and quantity accounting.

inventory.value: Advancement follows tolerance and refeeding risk.
inventory.support: 2016C3 and2020adultTable6; assess tolerance/refeeding without adding a rate protocol.

inventory.value: Track prescribed volume against actual delivery.
inventory.support: Safe2017Q6.7/Q6.11 actual versus prescribed volume; book quantity actually received.

inventory.value: Formula Selection and Hydration
inventory.support: Editorial heading matched to reviewed lesson topics.

inventory.value: Match formula composition to nutrient, volume, digestion, absorption, electrolyte, and tolerance needs; greater complexity does not establish greater benefit.
inventory.support: Safe2017Q5.1/Q5.2 and2016E1-E4/F1/I1-I2 formula physiology and setting-specific specialty caution; no universal greater benefit from complexity.

inventory.value: Polymeric and peptide-based formulas
inventory.support: Reviewed2023 composition tools distinguish intact versus hydrolyzed peptide composition; safe2017Q5.1/Q5.2 clinical selection.

inventory.value: Caloric density
inventory.support: Book nutrition labels state energy/volume; prior complete source tables and arithmetic retained.

inventory.value: Fiber and disease-specific products
inventory.support: 2016E1-E4/F1/I1-I2 specialty/fiber scope with ICU/patient qualifications.

inventory.value: Free water and renal solute load
inventory.support: Renal-solute physiological premise remains unsupported within authorized scopes; retain without closure while source-authorization question is pending.

inventory.value: Start with physiology and the nutrition prescription. Product marketing cannot substitute for an assessment of protein, calories, fluid, electrolytes, fiber, absorption, cost, and evidence.
inventory.support: Safe2017Q1.1/Table1 assessment, Q5.1/Q5.2 composition/clinical selection and2016E1-E4/F1/I1-I2 evidence-based rationale; cost/marketing do not establish benefit.

inventory.value: Polymeric formula is a reasonable starting point when digestion and absorption are intact.
inventory.support: Safe2017Q5.1/Q5.2 formula type based on digestion/absorption,2016E1 standard polymeric ICU starting point; qualified reasonable option, not universal formula mandate.

inventory.value: Calculate formula water from product composition and the volume actually delivered.
inventory.support: Book amount delivered plus product water composition; safe2017Q5.1 andQ7.2 patient-specific fluid plan.

inventory.value: Specialty formulas require a patient-specific rationale.
inventory.support: 2016E1-E4/F1/I1-I2 exclusions/exceptions and safe2017Q5.1/Q5.2; individualized rationale.

inventory.value: Formula volume and water volume are not interchangeable.
inventory.support: Book hypernatremia/extra water and labeled composition; water portion of formula differs from total volume.

inventory.value: Medication Administration Through Enteral Access
inventory.support: Editorial heading matched to reviewed lesson topics.

inventory.value: Safe medication delivery requires a dosage-form review, absorption-site review, drug-specific feeding plan, and flush sequence for every administration.
inventory.support: Book solid/liquid review and interactions; safe2017Q8.1/Q8.2/Q8.3 factors/flush sequence/hold distinction, not universal interval.

inventory.value: Do-not-crush formulations
inventory.support: Book printed162 incompatible altered release/enteric/buccal/sublingual/hazardous formulations; safe2017Q8.1/Q8.6.

inventory.value: Drug and nutrient interactions
inventory.support: Book nutrient/drug interactions and safe2017Q8.1/Q8.2 individualized separation.

inventory.value: Flush sequence
inventory.support: Safe2017Q8.2 pause, separate administrations, flushes and prompt restart when no interaction needs separation.

inventory.value: Tube site and dosage form
inventory.support: Book destination diagram and product-specific dosage-form review; safe2017Q8.1/Q8.3 actual tip and absorption/dissolution.

inventory.value: Do not ask only whether a tablet can fit through a tube. Ask whether the dosage form can be altered, whether the drug can be absorbed beyond the tube tip, and whether feeding changes exposure.
inventory.support: Book compatibility/product instructions and safe2017Q8.1/Q8.2 drug/formulation/tip/feeding review rather than physical fit alone.

inventory.value: Check product-specific instructions before altering or administering any dosage form through a tube.
inventory.support: Book complete printed162 explicitly addresses solid AND liquid compatibility and product instructions; safe2017Q8.1/Q8.2 liquid suitability and preparation.

inventory.value: Give medications separately from formula and from one another.
inventory.support: Book no drugs mixed into formula; safe2017Q8.2 each medication separately and no mixing due to physicochemical risks.

inventory.value: Use drug-specific feeding holds rather than a universal rule.
inventory.support: Safe2017Q8.2 interaction-specific extended separation versus routine administration pause; prior book interval discrepancy retained.

inventory.value: The tube tip can change drug absorption and effect.
inventory.support: Safe2017Q8.1/Q8.3 gastric conditions versus postpyloric absorption/dissolution; product-specific check.

inventory.value: Monitoring and Complication Prevention
inventory.support: Editorial heading matched to reviewed lesson topics.

inventory.value: Tolerance is a clinical pattern. Integrate delivered volume, symptoms, examination, stool, fluid balance, glucose, electrolytes, access integrity, and infection risk.
inventory.support: Safe2017Q11.1 whole-patient/delivery/access/laboratory monitoring,2016D1/D2/D6 and2020adultTable6; no symptom alone establishes cause.

inventory.value: Aspiration prevention
inventory.support: 2016D4/D5 and safe2017Q6.3/Q9.2 coordinated aspiration precautions.

inventory.value: Diarrhea and intolerance
inventory.support: 2016D1/D2/D6 symptoms and medication/formula/infectious differential.

inventory.value: Tube obstruction and displacement
inventory.support: Safe2017Q4.4/Q4.5 migration andQ7.1-Q7.3 patency; book medication obstruction.

inventory.value: Refeeding and metabolic monitoring
inventory.support: 2020adultTable6/pathophysiology and safe2017Q11.1 clinical/metabolic monitoring, no new numeric protocol.

inventory.value: When a problem appears, assess gastrointestinal, metabolic, mechanical, medication-related, and infectious causes. Respond promptly to urgent findings and reassess the feeding plan.
inventory.support: Safe2017Q11.1 and2016D1/D2/D6 differential assessment plus2020adultTable6 urgency for severe electrolyte findings; source-specific context remains in detailed lessons.

inventory.value: Aspiration prevention uses several coordinated measures.
inventory.support: 2016D4/D5 and safe2017Q9.2 multi-measure precautions; risk not eliminated.

inventory.value: A residual value must be interpreted in clinical context.
inventory.support: 2016D1/D2 with clinical signs and2023critical practice tool separate setting/limited evidence; no universal residual cutoff.

inventory.value: Assess medications as possible causes of diarrhea and tube obstruction.
inventory.support: 2016D6 medications among possible diarrhea causes; book printed162 blockage and safe2017Q8.1/Q8.2 formulation/preparation obstruction risk. No comparative incidence ranking.

inventory.value: Monitor what was delivered, not only what was ordered.
inventory.support: Safe2017Q6.7/Q6.11 andQ11.1 actual delivery monitoring.
